1.why: All ten screens are static, uncluttered single-card pages with no animations, moving images, or pop-ups visible anywhere.

2.why: Bold step headings, color-coded amber/green banners, and solid blue primary buttons make key elements prominent, though the long recovery token appears as small plain monospace text.

3.why: Each step presents exactly one labeled field and one primary button so the needed element is immediately locatable, though handling the 64-character token adds some effort.

4.why: Steps are shown one at a time with on-screen instructions, but the flow spans six stages and the password step imposes four rules including a '72 UTF-8 bytes (bcrypt limit)' condition.

5.why: No password manager integration, autofill option, or 'remember me' checkbox appears on any screen; all fields are manual entries only.

6.why: No saved accounts, saved emails, or other stored items are surfaced for recognition; only the demo token is automatically carried over between steps.

7.why: Instructions such as 'Enter your email address to begin' are short and plain, though jargon like 'UTF-8 bytes (bcrypt limit)' and 'Deterministic test code' appears.

8.why: No error message is shown in any of the ten steps, so there is no observed message that describes a problem and how to fix it.

9.why: The demo explicitly shows what to type, e.g., 'use the displayed test code 246810' and a pre-filled token field, though no example email or example password is provided.

10.why: No choice among password, code, or face login is offered; the flow forces a single fixed sequence of email, token, code, then new password.

11.why: Every screen presents at most one input and one or two buttons, so the number of simultaneous choices is minimal.

12.why: Green confirmation banners and the activity log state the result of each action, ending with 'Your password has been updated and the privacy statement acknowledgement has been recorded.'

13.why: Each step carries a short tip banner (e.g., token expiry warning, password advice) plus helper text under fields, though no help link or support contact is offered.

14.why: A 'Start over' button on the delivery step and 'Begin another recovery' on the final page allow retrying, though no in-error retry path is demonstrated.

15.why: All ten steps share the identical header, card layout, button styling, 'Keep your account safe' section, and activity log panel.
